4. The respondent bank has filed an affidavit-in-opposition specifically denying all materials allegations as well as stating the respondent's own case in reply. As regards the letters, minutes and the board memorandum it has generally been stated that these are matters of record. The bank has also denied that it did not follow the Bangladesh Bank guideline for NRBC bank. The bank has also asserted that the petitioners were absent in the concerned board meeting with leave granted to them and all these are matters of record. The bank has further maintains that the board resolutions were taken upon following the procedure laid down in the Articles of Association of the bank and the enquiry committee was validly formed to enquire into the allegations made against the petitioners, on the basis of the record available in the lawful custody of the bank. It has further been stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that the Respondent No. 1 i.e. NRB Commercial Bank Limited is a public company limited by shares and incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994, having Certificate of Incorporation No. C-107535/13 dated 20th February 2013 and is engaged in banking business as per provisions of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 (BCA) and 'has been continuing its banking business after obtaining license from the Bangladesh Bank under section 31 of the Bank Company Act, 1991; that NRB Commercial Bank Limited is established by the some highly motivated Bangladeshi expatriates who reside in different countries of the world, for the social and economic development of the motherland through their hard earned foreign currency; that the sponsors of the Bank have not only brought a huge investment into Bangladesh, but have also introduced the "state of the art technology" for building up a world standard Bank tailored towards meeting local developmental needs of the country; that it is stated that in the 39th Board Meeting held on 20-12-2015 the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 i.e. Mr Tamal SM Parvez and Mr Rafikul Islam Mia Arzoo acted violently and assaulted the Charmin of the Petitioner Bank demanding extension of service of 65 years old former Deputy Managing Director of the Bank, against the decision of the rest of the Board Members. The Chairman of the Bank, as Chairman of the Board, on 6-1-2016, 28-1-2016 and 7-2-2016 wrote letters to the Respondent No. 3 i.e. the Governor of the Bank informing the incident and requested for code of conduct or ethical guideline for the Board of Directors; that it is stated that in the 40th Board meeting held on 7-2-2016 the Petitioner No. 1 Mr Tamal SM Parvez brought an outsider with a Sub-Machine Gun in the Board Meeting and Petitioner No. 3 Mr Mohammed Adnan Imam was with Mr Parvez and aided him in that heinous Act. The Chairman of the Respondent Bank as Chairman of the Board of Directors and the Company secretary on 22-2-2016 and 23-2-2016 have filed 2 General Diaries (GD) with Motijheel Police Station and informed about the said incident; that it is stated that Mr Md Mujibur Rahman Shaikh, Joint Director of Financial Integrity and Customer Services Department (FICSD) and Mr KM Saimon Islam, Deputy Director were present in the 40th Board Meeting of the Respondent Bank held on 7-2-2016 as inspectors of Bangladesh Bank. In the said Board Meeting the Board has formed 2 (two) enquiry committees, one from the Board chaired by the Vice Chairman of the Bank and another from the Management chaired by the Managing Director-Cum-CEO. Mr Shaikh, Joint Director of FICSD, then on 17-2-2016 wrote a letter to the Chairman of the Board instructing to submit the enquiry report by 31-3-2016; that on 5-4-2016 the Chairman of the Board wrote a letter to the Executive Director of Bangladesh Bank informing that in the course of the enquiry it has been revealed that five Directors, namely Mr Adnan Imam as Chairman of the Executive Committee, Mr Rafikul Islam Mia Arzoo as Chairman of the Audit Committee, Mr Tamal SM Parvez as Chairman of the NRBC Bank Securities Limited, Mr Tushar Iqbal Rahman as Director and Mr Firoz Haider Khan as Directors of the Bank, in collusion with each other and with the support of former DMD & Head of Credit Committee of the Respondent Bank, have already availed benami/disguised loan of Taka 64,00,00,000 (sixty four crore) and attempted to pocket another Taka 165,00,00,000 (One hundred and sixty five Crore); that in the 41st and 42nd Board Meeting held on 7-3-2016 and 17-4-2016, respectively, the Board Hof Directors have removed the petitioners form their respective posts they held in the committees of the Bank and it was further agreed and unanimously resolved in the 42nd Board Meeting that the petitioners Mr Tamal S M Parvez, Mr Rafikul Mia Arzoo and Mr Adnan Imam shall not attend and participate in the activities of the Respondent Bank until completion of inquiry as against the Directors, their nominated alternative Directors and former DMD of the Respondent Bank for the unwanted incidents committed by them. (Annexure-DD to the petition). The Company Secretary on 19-4-2016 communicated the Minutes of the 42nd Board Meeting to the Bangladesh Bank; that it is stated that the 3rd Annual General Meeting of the Respondent Bank was held on 18-4-2016 and in the said AGM the shareholders of the Respondent Bank unanimously released Mr Tushar Iqbal Rahman and Mr Firoz Haider Khan from the Board of the Bank; that the Enquiry Committee in 1st meeting which was held on 28-4-2016 has resolved to complete the enquiry in three phases. First phase of the enquiry would be conducted based on available information/ documents and interview / question-answer sessions with the concerned persons. In the second phase, relevant documents/ information/answers would be examined and analyzed. In the third phase, all reports and updates would be combined to prepare the Final/ Comprehensive Report; that the Enquiry Committee accordingly conducted the enquiry and found that i) Mr Mohammed Adnan Imam ii) Mr Rafikul Islam Mia Arzoo iii) Mr Tamal SM Parvez iv) Mr AM Tushar Iqbal Rahman (nominated his father Mr Saidur Rahman as alternate director) and v) Mr Firoz Haider Khan (nominated his brother in law as alternate director) individually and jointly involved with swindling of public money of Taka 229 crore, took benami loans of Taka 64,00,00,000 crore, made suspicious foreign remittance of US$ 10 lac and committed other misdeeds; that on 7-7-2015 Petitioner No. 2 Mr Arzoo remitted USD 10,00,000 (One Million) from Moscow, Russia to credit his account lying with Petitioner Bank, Gulshan Branch, Dhaka. However on the same day i.e., 7-7-2015 Mr Arzoo with the assistance of the former Deputy Managing director of the Respondent Bank had remitted the said USD 10,00,000 (One Million) from his bank account to the account of Petitioner No. 3 Mr Adnan Imam in London, UK, against a loan contract signed by both Mr Arzoo and Mr Adnan for fixed return @ 22.00% per annum. Moreover, the said loan agreement between Mr Arzoo and Mr Adnan was executed on the same day i.e., 7-7-2015; that it is stated that 22.00% return p.a. in UK financial market is abnormally high because the base rate (LIBOR) in UK is less than 1.00 % whole the other side base rate (Bank Rate) in Bangladesh is 5.00%. The agreement between Mr Arzoo and Mr Adnan for 22.00% return and remittance of this huge fund of USD 10,00,000 (One Million) was highly suspicious; that upon inquiry it was found that the Respondent Bank was able to dismantle the attempts of swindling of public money of Taka 229 crore by stopping three benami loans of Taka 165 crore. However, the said 5(five) Directors managed to take away Taka 64 crore deceiving the Bank against 5(five) benami loans namely (1).VOSD, (2). Ornita Agro, (3). NES Trading, (4). Pubali Construction and (5). Lanta Services. They tied up with each other centering a common business entity namely Royal Denim Limited (RDL) and transacted with each other linking their 5 (five) Benami Loans. They did not give any declaration before the enquiry about their common interest business/ benami loans/ transactions with the said benami loan accounts; that on 23-6-2016 the Chairman of the Board wrote letter to the Bangladesh Bank informing about resolutions  of the 41st and 42nd Board Meeting and the misdeeds of the said Directors and requested permission to form an Ethical Consultative Group (ECG) comprising of dignified bankers like, any former Governor of Bangladesh Bank, any former Deputy Governor of Bangladesh Bank and any former MD of Commercial Bank to guide the petitioner bank to prepare Ethical Guideline and Conducts (EGC) for the Directors of the Bank; that it is stated that in the 43rd Board Meeting held on 11-5-2016 the chairman of the Enquiry Committee submitted 1st Meeting Minutes of the Enquiry Committee. The 44th Board Meeting held on 30-6-2016 and in the said meeting the Board unanimously decided to relieve the Petitioners from the Board until adjustment of disguised loans of Taka 61 crore and completion of the enquiry of following the BRPD Circular-4 dated 23-2-2014 Clause No. 3.4 and to give scope to the named directors either to adjust their benami loans or to stay out from the Board (Annexure-OO1 to the Petition). The Bank meantime recovered benami loans of Taka 3 crore out of disbursed amount of Taka 64 crore; that the Company Secretary of the Petitioner Bank wrote a letter bearing ref No. NRBC/HO/BS/2016-123 dated 13-7-2016 to Petitioner No. 3 i.e. Mr Mohammad Adnan Imam requesting to adjust disguised loans availed of from the Petitioner Bank namely loans of Pubali General Construction Ltd. for Taka 9 Crore and NES Trading Ltd. for Taka 19 Crore and the Chairman of Pubali General Construction Ltd. and authorized signatory of the NES Trading Ltd. referring to the letter No. NRBC/HO/BS/2016-123 dated 13-7-2016, in response, wrote letters dated 17-7-2016 informing that they have already adjusted the loan amount, which show direct involvement of Mr Mohammad Adnan Imam in Pubali General Construction Ltd. loan for Taka 9 Crore and NES Trading Ltd. loan for Taka 19 Crore; that the Respondent Bank has recovered Taka 45 crore out of disbursed amount of Taka 64 crore and not yet been able to recover remaining loans of Taka 19 crore. As decided in the AGM/ the Board, the Bank suspended distribution of dividends of said two former Directors i.e. Mr Tushar Iqbal Rahman and Mr Firoz Haider Kahn for the year 2015 and attached their shares until full adjustment of benami loans; that subsequently on 14-7-2016 the time for submitting inquiry report was extended till 31-7-2016 and the Enquiry Committee in the 45th Board Meeting held on 24-7-2016 submitted its report to the Board; that the Enquiry Reports prepared by International Division, dated 17-8-2016 and 6-9-2016, opined that remittance was suspicious because of its purpose and duration. Mr Arzoo could not give any clear explanation as to why the fund was not directly sent to UK from Russia and for what reasons it was routed through Bangladesh and who deposited the amount for a while in his NRBC Bank's account. Mr Arzoo and Mr Adnan were the Chairmen of the Audit Committee and the Executive Committee, respectively, when this financial transaction took place; that as per instruction of the Board of Directors of the Respondent Bank dated 8-7-2016 the Internal Control and Compliance Division (ICCD) of the Respondent Bank on 22-8-2016 submitted its enquiry report about the disguised loan accounts of the Petitioners and two other former Directors of the Bank, one former DMD and others. Similarly the Support Service & Branch Division (SSD) of the Respondent Bank had also submitted their report on the contract executed by the Petitioner No. 3, Mr Adnan Imam, EC Chairman, for renting his own premises for the Banani Branch of the Bank at 1st, 2nd and 3rd Floor of the AWR Tower at Road No. 11, House 99, Banani, Dhaka and the Petitioner No. 3 is the Managing Director of AWR Real Estate Limited. The Petitioner No. 3 also availed the Decoration Contract of the Banani Branch costing 1,00,74,090 of the Respondent Bank under the name of M/s Adrita Trading; that the Petitioner No. 2 Mr Rafikul Islam Mia Arzoo was Chairman of Audit Committee when the benami loan issue came into the notice of the Bank. Bank repeatedly requested him to give audit instruction in this regard. But he did not comply with the request. Bank at last, wrote to him on 18-9-2016. However the Petitioner No. 2 during his incumbency as Chairman of the Audit Committee initiated mutual business with Alternate Director Mr AM Saidur Rahman and Alternate Director Mr AKM Mostafizur Rahman and they invested in a textile company namely Royal Denim Limited. Mr Saidur Rahman (former Alternate Director of the Bank) is the Chairman of Royal Denim Limited (RDL). He was involved with multi-layer transactions to hide the actual source fund. This conduct was absolute violation of the BRPD Circular No. 4 dated 23-2-2014; that it is stated that Mr Saidur and Mr Mostafiz took Benami loans from the Bank on account of VOSD and they transferred a sum of Taka 30 lac on 14-1-2015 from VOSD to Royal Denim. Mr Arzoo, Mr Saidur, Mr Mostafiz, VOSD and Royal Denim are inter-connected with each other in direct/indirect/disguised manner for common business interest; that the Petitioner No. 3 Mr Mohammed Adnan Imam (former Chairman of Executive Committee) was beneficiary of benami agri loan on account of Ornita Agro for Taka 3 core. He diverted this Agri fund to his share business company namely IPE Capital. Such diversion of fund from Agri loan to share business is clear violation of Agri loan sanction terms. Agri loan is allocated for poor farmers at a very low /concessional interest rate as directed by Bangladesh Bank. Mr Adnan diverted this Agri loan fund in NCC Bank Banani Branch in his share business company namely IPE Capital Limited against three cheques bearing numbers 38908, 38909 and 38910 all dated 24-4-2014 for Taka 1 crore each total Taka 3 crore; that according to BRPD Circular-11 dated 27-10-2013 and BRPD Circular No. 4 dated 23-2-2014, Company Act-1994 and Articles of Association of the Bank the directors obtained loans from the Bank would be disqualified automatically and thus their Offices will be vacated. A memo bearing No. 04/46 was placed before the board in 46th board meeting held on 8-9-2016 giving information of benami loan of VOSD. The Board of Directors considering all the enquiry reports and letter of the Governor of Bangladesh Bank to the Finance Minister unanimously resolved to recommend vacate the directorship of the alleged directors (Annexure-Y to the inquiry Report); that it is stated that the Petitioners individually have filed Company Matter Nos. 192, 193 and 194 of 2016 under section 85(3) of the Companies Act 1994 and subsequently Company Matter Nos. 192 and 193 and 194 of 2016 were dismissed for non-prosecution. However during pendency of the Company Matter No. 194 of 2016, the same Petitioners filed the instant Company Matter and after hearing this Court was pleased to admit the said Matter on 9-11-2016 and passed an interim order and being aggrieved with the said interim Order the Respondent Bank filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3655 of 2016 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division and after hearing the Hon'ble Appellate Division pleased to stay the interim order and directed the Respondent No. 1 Bank to file the enquiry report before this Bench on or before 31st December of 2016 and in compliance with the said Order of the Hon'ble Appellate Division the Respondent Bank have filed Affidavit in Compliance along with the detailed enquiry report (Annexure-3 to the affidavit in compliance); that the it is humbly submitted that the Board of Directors of the Respondent Bank is comprised with 20 directors and the Respondent No. 2 as Chairman of the Board do not have any power to adopt or pass any resolution without vote or consent of the other Directors of the Board; that the Petitioners have failed to establish that, the Board acted discriminatorily against them or have passed such resolution which discriminates or likely to discriminate the interest of the Petitioners or the affairs of the Bank are being conducted or the powers of the Directors of the Board are being exercised in an manner prejudicial to the Petitioners as such the instant Company Matter is liable to be dismissed; In addition, the bank has also filed supplementary affidavit and the same do form part of the substantive affidavit-in-opposition. The bank has attached to it the certificate of incorporation No. C-107505/13 dated 20-3-2013, certificate for commencement of business being No. C-107535/13 dated 20-2-2013. The bank license under reference BRPD(P-3 /745(60)/2013-1158 dated 10-3-2013 and to establish offices for the purpose of doing banking vide reference VRPD(P-3) 745(16)/ 2013-1189, permitted to open banks for doing business of banking vide license No. BL/DA 10885/2013 dated 7-4-2013 and Gazette Notification No. BRPD(P-3)/744(93)/2013-1379 dated 25-3-2013 published in Bangladesh Gazette on 28-3-2013, whereby the respondent bank was listed as a scheduled bank. 

 6. Mr Mahbubey Alam and Mr Kamal-ul-Alam appeared with Mr AM Aminuddin, Mr SM Moniruzzaman with Mr Abdur Rokib, Mr M. Shakhawat Hosain and Mrs. Shahanaj Akther appeared for the respondent No. 1. They have placed the petition, the affidavit-in-opposition, the 3 (three) volume Comprehensive Enquiry Report (CER in brief) submitted before this Court within the time frame fixed by the Appellate Division. Having drawn my attention to the pleadings of the parties and to the documents annexed to the same as well as to the comprehensive enquiry report (CER) submitted by the respondent bank, the learned Advocate for the respondent Bank submits that the instant petition has filed by the petitioners under section 233 of the Companies Act, 1994, to protect their status and interest as director qua, while section 233 of the Act contemplates the interest for only of the members. Their next contention is that this petition under section 233 of the Companies Act, 1994, has been filed with collateral purpose to prevent the bank from taking appropriate actions against the petitioners even though they have acted in violation of their duties and the law, thereby exposed the bank to a huge financial loss by obtaining benami loans, by entering into tenancy agreement and also an agreement to decorate Banani Branch of the bank and also by resorting to money laundering. The learned Advocates next points out that the petitioner's intention to abuse the process of the Court will be evident from the fact of filing their 3 similar petitions under section 81(2) read with section 85(3) of the Act. These 3 petitions were filed respectively by these 3 petitioners on 21-8-2016, 28-8-2016 and 29-8-2016 and were registered as Company Matter Nos. 192 of 2016, 193 of 2016 and 194 of 2016, respectively. These 3 company matters were dismissed as being not pressed on 7-12-2016, 6-12-2016 and 7-1-2017, that is during the pendency of the instant petition filed under section 233 of the Act. As such, he asserts that, the instant petition has also been filed in continuation of the multiplicity of futile proceedings initiated by them with intend to suppress their misdeeds and unfair conducts that have seriously prejudiced the interest of the bank. In the facts and circumstances of this case, the learned Advocate next moved to persuade the Court that the petitioners were not in fact removed by the board of directors. Rather the petitioners have ceased to be the directors of the bank by operation of law i.e. according to the provision of clause (c), subsection (1) of section 103 of the Companies Act, 1994 read with clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 108 of the Act. Besides, he maintains that the petitioners have become disqualified owing to violation of the provisions of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 and of the BRDP Circulars No. 11 dated 27-10-2013 and No. 4 dated 23-2-2014. He vehemently argues that the case stated in the affidavit-in-opposition about the benami loans availed of by the petitioners, as proved by the materials on record, as well as by the statements of accounts comprising the Comprehensive Enquiry Report (CER) submitted in 3 (three) volumes by the respondent Bank. The learned Advocate has pointed out that the statement of accounts maintained by the bank in the ordinary course of its business, annexed to the pleadings as well as to the enquiry report, clearly put on record the benami loans availed of by the petitioners through the aforementioned 5(five) entities used as their proxies. He was then prompt to add that these reports were submitted, based on the findings of the Enquiry Committee and upon specific allegations of availing disguised loan and for engaging in suspicious transactions by the petitioners working as a clique and operating in multilayer transaction. Indeed, the learned Advocate proceeds on, that taking advance of the office of the then Chairman of the Audit Committee and of the Executive Committee and also of the office of directors of the bank, the petitioners have used their power and position to secure their own interest by availing loan for their own businesses carried in the benami of the firms/companies in which they have personal interest. Therefore, the petitioners have indirectly done the same acts and deeds which they are not legally permitted to do directly. It has further been pointed out that the benami transactions of the petitioners are on record and that they have admitted the same in writing letters as well as by their conduct. On the allegations of doing similar acts, he further submits, 2 (two) other directors, namely Mr Feroj Haider Khan and Mr Tushar Iqbal Rahman, have resigned from the board as per decision taken in the 3rd AGM and their shares are kept under attachment till the benami loan is adjusted by them. On behalf of the respondent Bank it has also been maintained that the leave were granted to the petitioners from attending the board meeting as per their request as will be evident from the record. Besides, he proceeds on, that, the 45th board resolution dated 24-7-2016 and 46th board resolution dated 8-11-2016 were taken in the interest of the bank for recovery of the benami loans of the petitioners. But the petitioners have resorted to these multiplicities of proceedings to conceal their acts and deeds and to avoid prosecution under the Money Laundering Act. They are, therefore, clearly disqualified, as per the AoA and the law, to sit in the bank as directors. Accordingly, the learned Advocate submits that this petition bears no merit and the same is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 9. Therefore, it is the individual interest of each member of a company, who holds the qualifying shares, to enjoy, amongst other, the right and privilege to be elected or to be appointed as director in a company, whether as a member or as a nominee of a member (in the case of corporate members) and to continue in their office until the same should fall vacant or is determined in accordance with the provisions of law. 

 16. As such, I find that the board has brought specific allegations against the petitioners and against other directors too. The allegations were brought to their notice and an Enquiry Committee formed by the Board. The Enquiry Committee has interrogated and interviewed the petitioners in detail, on the allegations brought against them and has meticulously examined all the documentary evidence, entries and information’s on record. Enquiry Committee has submitted its report before the Board and the Board, having taken into account the report along with the relevant materials on record, has taken the measure the measures as recorded in resolutions, as quoted above. Now, the next question is, whether the measures taken in the above quoted resolutions vis-a-vis the premise in which they have adopted would attract the mischief of section 233 and if the company remedies are available to the petitioners, under that section. 

 21. Therefore, specific allegations of taking disguised or benami loans have arisen in this case. 

 22. In the case of a disguised or benami loan the actual debtor contrives a mechanism so that his connection or involvement with such loan or transaction cannot be easily traced with or established. Such facts or contrivances are especially within the knowledge of the person who is alleged to have availed the benami loan. Therefore, as per provisions of section 106 of the Evidence Act, 1872, the burden lies upon the person who is alleged to have obtained the benami loan to prove that he or she is not actual debtor, particularly, when the preponderance of evidence on record supports the claim that he/she is the actual debtor. 

 39. As regards further allegations against Mr Rafiqul Islam Mia Arzoo, the respondent Bank has placed page 329 of Vol.-2 of the CER, wherein it has reproduced the statements of account No. 001 of VOSD (an NCO), maintained with Gulshan Branch of the respondent bank, that records that on 14-1-2015 an amount of Taka 30 lacs was transferred to the CD Account No. 419 of RDL, maintained with the Principal Branch of the respondent bank. Further case of the respondent bank is that, admittedly Rafiqul Islam Mia Arzoo is a shareholder in RDL. Therefore, I find prima-facie evidence that Rafiqul islam Mia Azroo has obtained loan by using the names of VOSD and RDL. 

 42. The Bank, I am of the further opinion, that as trustee of the depositors money and since standing as a debtor in relation to it's clients money, must not be left to suffer a protracted litigation or loss of it's assets without any equitable or legal security in the circumstances like this case. In the case of Champagne Perrier- Joeut SA vs HH Finch [1982] 3 All ER 713, the court, in view of the. AOA giving the company paramount lien over his (the debtor's) shares held that, the company had at all material times a lien over his (the debtor's) shares, and that lien took priority over an equitable charge (though the company had at no stage made a loan in the strict sense of the term). 

 43. Besides, the bank, or any other company, is well authorized to record vacation of office of a director as per provisions of section 108 of the Companies Act, 1994, if the facts, with which the bank is well posted with relevant knowledge, so justify. For effectuating a vacation of office of a director no resolution is required to be taken by the board to the effect that the office of a director is hereby vacated, inasmuch as, it happens ipso facto or by operation of law. The resolution, in the case of a vacation of office of directors, shall only record that such vacation of office of within the named director has taken place as per provision of law and/or Articles of Association, and shall submit a Form XII with the Registrar, Joint Stock Companies and Firms, and shall ensure other compliance, if any. 

 48. Be that as it may, from the manner of transaction recorded by the bank in its books of account and having considered the minutes of board meeting, the materials placed before the Court, the pleading of the parties as well as 3 Volumes CER, there is apparent basis before this Court to record a finding that the measures taken against the petitioners and in respect of the questioned transaction and dealings are all warranted in the fact and circumstances of this case and the bank is as much competent to as it is under a statutory duty to take such measures. Besides, the circumstance does not disclose any personal grudge against the petitioners. Hence, I have no hesitation to hold that, this case does not, and similar case will not, attract the mischief of section 233 of the Act. 

 50. In the case of vacation office, the question of taking approval will not arise. Now, the question is whether in case of removal of the petitioner's approval or consent of Bangladesh Bank is required or not. 

 54. The jurisdiction to give interpretation of law lies within the exclusive province of the Court. This position of law has been set at rest by series of decisions. Bangladesh Bank or any other authority, invested with power under the provisions of any statute or other law, cannot give meaning to any word used in an statute, either to confer it a jurisdiction not given to or to refuse to exercise a jurisdiction vested in it. Interpretation of sub-section (4) of section 15 have been given in view of the issue raised in the case and as necessitated for complete adjudication of all the issues relevant for disposal of this matter and, therefore, the Bangladesh Bank and other authorities shall issue necessary order or circular in the light of the interpretation given above, as required by Article 112 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Besides, this judgment shall be binding on all Courts subordinate to this Division, as per Article 111 of the Constitution. 

 55. As regards the allegation of entering inside the bank with armed person, some CC TV footage clearly shows appearance of armed persons inside the bank. The banks always put security personnel’s or guards for its own security. Entering with armed personnel inside the bank in any circumstances or in any case should be taken seriously as it creates a serious threat to safety and security of the cashes and the valuable instruments kept in or handled inside the bank as well as to the customers and employees of the bank. The Magistrate Court and the law enforcing agencies must take up such incident seriously and shall respond to immediately. No personal Gunman or personal body guard should be allowed to enter inside the bank. The bank shall arrange and take steps to ensure safety and security of all and everything inside the bank as well as in the board meetings, and the general meetings, if so required, by issuing necessary office orders. The banks should also amend their Articles of Association, providing for vacation of office of a Director (1) who threatens to disturb or is likely to disturb the peaceful atmosphere or the orderly situation in any board meeting or of any general meeting and, (2), if so disclosed by the bank's record, who is found to have taken "benami loan", as additional grounds, which the Bank is authorized to include vide, section 108(2) of the Companies Act, by adopting a special resolution. 

 (I) The 44th, 45th and the 46th board resolutions of NRBC, so far as it relates to 'relieve' the petitioners from the board of directors, is hereby cancelled. Therefore, till continuation in their offices, the petitioners shall be entitled to receive notices of the board meetings, however, on condition that, whether taken up singly or otherwise, they shall not remain present in any board meeting in which any agenda relating to or concerning them or any one of them is scheduled to be discussed or may otherwise come up, or is taken up as miscellaneous item for discussion in the Bank's Board of Directors,
